newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin shrugs off local election setbacks.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin shrugs off local election setbacks.

text.p: The Kremlin shrugged off its latest setbacks in regional elections on Tuesday and said Russian President Boris Yeltsin expected good cooperation with the new local leaders regardless of their political leanings.
Presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky singled out the new governors of the Amur and Tula regions for mention after their victories in elections at the weekend.

"The change of leadership in these regions was to be expected. The social and economic situation was too tense in both," Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing, blaming the defeats on the poor work of the outgoing governors.
He said that the victors' being backed by the opposition "does not mean they do not need close and constructive cooperation with the president and the government".
"The president of Russia is for constructive cooperation with any administration, regardless of its political inclinations," Yastrzhembsky said.
Communist-backed Vasily Starodubtsev, one of the leaders of a hardline coup against Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev in 1991, was elected governor of the Tula region south of Moscow on Sunday.
Communist Anatoly Belonogov won the governorship of the Amur region bordering China and, like Starodubtsev, secured a seat in the upper house of parliament, the Federation Council.
In another setback for the Kremlin on Sunday, nationalist Dmitry Rogozin won a seat in the State Duma lower house of parliament in an election in the southern region of Voronezh.

The opposition victories came at a time of widespread discontent, with long delays in payment of wages and pensions which have prompted trade unions to call a day of nationwide protests and strikes on Thursday.
